subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics, stored cron shape, CLI flags, and upgrade behavior, and repository policy treats config/default additions as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit opt-in cron `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, protocol, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Decline cron `every` phase or prime behavior for now and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for built-in anti-herd protection.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Define a larger heartbeat and cron prime-cadence feature with migration, observability, and compatibility requirements before implementation.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit opt-in cron `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, protocol, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-history signal on the cron stagger and schedule-option surfaces that define the remaining public API boundary.
